summary: Yaroslav Vasilkov specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1961–1967) and held positions at Saint Petersburg State University, the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (~1973–2005), and Kunstkamera/Peter the Great Museum (~2005).

Yashaswini Chandra is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She held positions at Sahapedia (2011–2018), SOAS (2011–2012), Jawaharlal Nehru University (2012–2013), Ashoka University (2019), and the University of Edinburgh (2023).

Yasuaki Nara was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno at the University of Tokyo and attended the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Komazawa University and the Soto Zen Research Center.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD). His posts include the National Museum of Ethnology, UC Berkeley, Toyo Bunko, and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Yasuhiko Sueki is a scholar in philosophy and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1980). He held a post as professor emeritus at Komazawa University (~2018).

Yasuhiro Okazaki works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Hiroshima University, studying under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and has held teaching posts at Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Hiroshima Prefectural Takamiya high schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library (~1988–1989). He held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He has held posts at Kyoto University and Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1978–2000).

Yasuke Ikari is an Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts at Kindai University, the National Museum of Ethnology, Harvard University, and Kyoto University.

Yasuko Kojima is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She has held posts as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yasumasa Sekine works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. His academic posts include Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasunori Ejima was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held positions at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Nagaoka University of Technology, and the University of Tokyo.

Yasuo Deguchi specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After doctoral studies at Kyoto University, he served at the Nagoya Institute of Technology, Kyoto University—including as professor and dean—and ZEN University, and founded the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy.
Yasuo Goto is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held teaching posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1991 and 2006) and Shuchiin University (attested 2006).
Yasuo Inamoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Nara National Museum (~1997–2002) and Kyoto University (~2003).

Yasuo Matsunami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano and held positions as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1992–2006) and advisor to the Śrāvakabhūmi Study Group.
Yasuo Sano is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Yasuo Yuasa was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo, University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.
